name: chair-decides-scored-only
expectation: ADL business rule ChairOnScoredOnly: a panel decision is recorded only by an account holding the panel chair role, only for a proposal with an open adjudication case (which exists only once the proposal is scored), only once, and an award only when no integrity hold is on the case.

claim.clause: A panel decision is recorded only by an account holding the panel_chair role, only for a proposal with an open adjudication case (which exists only once the proposal is scored), only once, and an award only when no integrity hold is on the case.

boundary.statement: The recording of a panel decision and what follows from it: every write in src/** that records a panel decision (either outcome), every publish of the decision fact, every write that moves a proposal to awarded or declined, and every runtime entry point into the decision writes, with requests handled one at a time.

excludes.what: the demo seed's calls of recordDecision (src/seed.ts)
excludes.why: demo data, never run when NODE_ENV=production; no case drives it and the performer guard (the route) does not apply to it

excludes.what: same action, other rules — NOT judged here: ADL EnvelopeNotExceeded (BDL i-q009), i-q014 AwardIsTheRequestedAmount, the open question u-q001 ConflictAfterDecision, and when a late conflict must place a hold (BDL r-q013 AwardHeldOnLateConflict)
excludes.why: each is its own claim about the panel decision; a level on ChairOnScoredOnly says nothing about them, so the award is not 'fully governed' by this result. Of the hold, only this rule's clause is judged: an award is not recorded while a hold is on the case
it screens a proposal in; it records no panel decision

excludes.what: the read model ovs_proposal and notifications
excludes.why: projections fed by the decision fact; they record a decision, they cannot make one. Their writes are still scanned as outcome writes and must lie in a handler of the fact

excludes.what: two decision requests for one proposal in flight at once
excludes.why: the cases send one request at a time; the conditional claim of the case (UPDATE adj_case … WHERE status IN ('awaitingDecision','reconsider'), one row changed) and the one-decision-per-proposal key are observed statically, not raced

excludes.what: how an integrity hold comes to be on a case, and how it is released
excludes.why: the rule speaks only of an award while a hold is on the case; the hold is placed here through the conflict route, and its release is an open owner decision (ADR-005)

scope.discovery: Lex src/**: every SQL write to adj_decision, every UPDATE of adj_case to 'decided', every publish of ProposalAwarded/ProposalDeclined (a computed event type is unresolved), and every move of a proposal to awarded/declined — through the status channel transition() or its forwarder react() with a literal target, or literal SQL. Every call of a function holding a decision write is an entry point (an HTTP registration named by method, URL and declared access). Non-literal SQL must resolve, else the scope is incomplete.
scope.concurrencyStatement: not covered: every case sends one decision request at a time; no case races two decisions for one proposal

assumptions.statement: The claim is the ADL rule's whole statement. The business model states three of its parts for the decision RecordPanelDecision (ac-q019, rule r-q008): the verifier reads its compiled condition and precondition (Proposal is Scored) and reports them beside the guards as corroboration; the level does not rest on them.
"An account holding the panel_chair role" is the role the route's access list names (panelChair, scope.actorRoles; BDL ac-q019 mayPerform PanelChair). The mapping is stated here, not inferred.
"Only once" is checked as a single decision per proposal: the decided guard, a conditional claim of the case, and adj_decision keyed by proposal.

An adj_case row exists only for a scored proposal: it is opened only in the ProposalScored handler. The scored guard is 'refuse without a case'; the correspondence check verifies the case is opened nowhere else.

A proposal's status is written only through transition() (the one UPDATE of sub_proposal.status, parametric); every outcome is a call of it, or of a forwarder, with a literal target status. Any other form is unresolved.

Cases set up their world through the implementation's own test harness (tests/support/harness.ts), in-process (Fastify inject) against an isolated SQLite file with a manual clock. The act under test — the HTTP route — and the state read — adj_decision and sub_proposal.status — are the verifier's.
Guards and correspondence are recognised textually (lexed, not parsed); a refactor they do not recognise reads as 'not shown', never as 'violated'.

The `reached` paths are what V8 precise BLOCK coverage reports executing during the act alone — the request and the delivery of the events it published; setup excluded. A site is reached when its code ran; a continuation after an early throw is read with the count V8 gives it. A proposal outcome applied by a handler built from a factory call is reached when a function passed to that call ran. Observed by the runtime, not declared.

"An open adjudication case (which exists only once the proposal is scored)": a case is an adj_case row, opened only on ProposalScored (checked statically); the edge of scored is a proposal with two of its three reviews submitted.
An integrity hold is adj_case.integrity_hold being set; the cases place it the way the implementation does, by declaring a reviewer's conflict after scoring through POST /api/conflicts.

checks.statement: The in-scope paths: decision writes, decision-fact publishes, outcome writes and their entry points; complete only when nothing is unresolved.
the chair awards a scored proposal: the decision is recorded and the proposal is awarded
the chair declines a scored proposal: the decision is recorded and the proposal is declined
with an integrity hold on the case, the chair's decline is still recorded: the hold stops an award, not a decision

a program officer, an operator, an applicant, a reviewer and an unverified reviewer are each refused on a scored proposal; nothing is recorded or published. Counts only when its control, chair-decides-scored, passed on the same route
the chair is refused on a proposal under review (code not_scored); nothing is recorded or published. Counts only when its control, chair-decides-scored, passed on the same route
with an integrity hold on the case, the chair's award is refused (code integrity_hold); nothing is recorded or published. Counts only when its control, chair-decides-scored, passed on the same route
the edge of scored: with two of the three reviews submitted the chair is refused (code not_scored). Counts only when its control, chair-decides-scored (all three submitted), passed on the same route
the edge of only once: after a first decision the second is refused (code already_decided) and the first stands. Counts only when its control, chair-declines-scored, passed on the same route
Each write that moves a proposal to awarded or declined lies in a handler of the decision fact (ProposalAwarded / ProposalDeclined).

Every in-scope path is constrained: every entry is a route with a declared access; the scored and once guards precede every decision write; the fact is published only by the guarded function; outcomes are applied only on the fact.

each part of the rule has its guard: only the panel chair role is admitted on the route; a decision needs a case, opened only on ProposalScored; a decided case is refused and one decision per proposal is the store's key; an award on a held case is refused before anything is committed

violations.statement: the rule is not enforced on the decision path: an account that is not a panel chair records a decision
the edge of only once is misplaced: a second decision is admitted and replaces the first
an award is recorded while an integrity hold is on the case

challenges.statement: the panel-decision route also admits a Program Officer
recordDecision no longer refuses a decided case, its conditional claim admits one, and the decision row is replaced: a second decision is recorded over the first
recordDecision no longer refuses an award on a held case
